derivation_rule: Every `verified_stages` block below is the manifest's own row for that case, which `compiler/tests/ct_corpus.rs` independently rederives from its own dispatch and refuses drift on. Nothing here is a second hand-kept copy.

what_changed_and_what_did_not.changed: CT07's artifact and route. Wave 30's `CT07-WRITE-REMAP` mapped the case onto two write authorities over disjoint ranges of one buffer held by ONE SEQUENTIAL ENTRY's bindings, and named the gap in its own semantic profile: `NOT two threads; the task-crossing half is residual WRITE-LEND-TASKS`. Wave 31 crossed the spawn boundary with the lease; wave 36's `WRITE-LEND-TASKS-EXERCISE` let a worker body write through it and ran two threads writing distinct bytes of one int32_t under ASan/UBSan/LSan. CT07's scenario word `independently` therefore has a two-thread artifact for the first time, and the case now rests on it: route sequential -> task, verdict mode sequential_sanitized -> native_heap_scenarios, executor run_sequential_sanitized -> run_native_heap_scenarios.
what_changed_and_what_did_not.did_not_change: Any count. CT07 was mapped before this card and is mapped after it; mapped stays 46 of 50, sanitized-native stays 10 of 46 (CT07 was already in SANITIZED_GATED_CASES and remains there, one gated case leaving the sequential runner and arriving at the heap runner), and proof stays 3 of 46. Nothing was promoted, nothing was newly mapped, and no unmapped case became mapped.
what_changed_and_what_did_not.why_this_is_not_merely_a_relabel: The two-thread reading is not a description of the same evidence. Under the sequential mapping the four stores were statements of one thread, interleaved in source order, and no thread ever ran concurrently with another; the disjointness that mattered was between two BINDINGS. Under this mapping the two write authorities are held by two OS threads created by thrd_create, live simultaneously (the observation shows QCORE_BUFFER_LEASE 1 and QCORE_BUFFER_LEASE 2 both taken before either byte is written), and the disjointness that matters is between two THREADS' footprints, decided by ownership::axes_overlap called from the scoped-task ledger. Those are different facts about different programs, and only the second one is the scenario's.

boundaries_published_not_papered_over.no_thread_sanitizer_evidence: There is NO race-detector evidence for this case, and none is claimed. ThreadSanitizer cannot run any program this route emits - lease or not - measured in wave 36 on three programs including a published example that holds no lease, all faulting at the identical address and pc (TASK-ROUTE-TSAN-SEGV). So `two threads write distinct memory locations and this is not a data race` is carried by C11 3.14, by the ASan/UBSan/LSan run, and by the allocation identity - and NOT by a race detector. A sibling card TASK-ROUTE-TSAN is working the residual in parallel; if it lands, the addition to this case would be a TSan row asserting silence on the flagship, which is the one direct observation the case currently lacks.
boundaries_published_not_papered_over.extent: The payload is one int32_t, so BUFFER_PAYLOAD_BYTES is 4 and the two `halves` are two bytes each. The scenario says `array halves`; four bytes is a thin array. That is residual WRITE-LEND-TASKS-EXTENT, inherited unchanged from wave 31 and not closed here.
boundaries_published_not_papered_over.platform: Linux arm executed. The same runner compiles on macOS and the manifest's host_gate says so; no Windows or Apple run is claimed for this case (WRITE-LEND-EXERCISE-WINDOWS-RUN covers the card-side program on the same footing).
boundaries_published_not_papered_over.one_writer_per_worker: Each worker writes exactly one byte, because the ledger admits at most one write lease per worker and the route admits a check-time-constant index only. The scenario's `mutated` is therefore one store per party, not a loop.

CT42.scenario: Two descriptors share an underlying logical state
CT42.re_measured_on_this_tree: Both arms, at wave-37 base 0f6eb0a6. ARM A (the C twin, CT-CTWIN-DESCRIPTOR): the contract loader still refuses an int-typed resource identity at crates/qcore-contract/src/contract_loader.rs:757-759, `if result != ResourceReturnMode::None && !return_type.starts_with("ptr<")` -> `owned result requires a pointer return type`, which is what produces the verbatim refusal wave 9, wave 17 and wave 35 all recorded. The refusal is pinned by compiler/tests/contract_loader.rs::every_abi_scalar_is_a_borrowed_only_projection, so it is load-bearing rather than incidental. ARM B (the socket cell, CT42-CELL-UNROUTED): grep for derive_socket_cells and footprint_program across crates/ and compiler/ finds callers in crates/qcore-core/tests/unit/ only - nothing in the frontend, nothing in the checker, nothing in compile_files. Unchanged from wave 35.
CT42.why_still_unmapped: Neither arm can be mapped by a mapping lane, and each fails for its own reason. ARM A is out of this lane's scope by measurement, not by preference: discharging it starts at one line of crates/qcore-contract but cascades into qcore-schemas (ResourceReturnMode records only nullability, and a descriptor's failure value is -1, not null, so the failure arm is not expressible at all), into crates/qcore-core/src/extern_call.rs:790-801, and into crates/qcore-c-gateway/src/legacy_declared_abi.rs together with the projection's pointer-keyed identity tracking. This lane's charter forbids C gateway source changes and says to map only if every word is carried without a gateway change; by this measurement ARM A needs one. ARM B fails constraint 23 directly: the model, the Lean and the Q664 refusal all exist, but no .qcore statement asks the disjointness question and no source route reaches the deriver, so a CT42 row on that arm would name stages the harness CANNOT EXECUTE. Wiring it is a route card (new source syntax plus checker wiring), not a mapping lane.

CT10.scenario: Adjacent bit-fields in one memory location
CT10.re_measured_on_this_tree: The concurrency half is present, byte-granular and source-reachable: LeaseRange / WriteLeased / OverlappingLeases in crates/qcore-core/src/scoped_tasks.rs, deciding through ownership::axes_overlap (crates/qcore-core/src/ownership.rs:145), reachable from source by the `lend NAME LOW..HIGH` capture - and this lane's own CT07 remap is that mechanism executing. The sub-byte half is representable in exactly ONE model-level module and unreachable from any program: FieldStorage::BitfieldUnit { unit, bit_offset, bit_width } (crates/qcore-core/src/disjoint_footprint.rs:99-103) is the only bit-addressed type in the workspace, and its own documentation says the declared bit range `never participates in the disjointness decision` (:214-216). FootprintExport::SharedMemoryLocation (:229-231) exists precisely so a bit-field unit cannot be exported to a concurrency checker as an interval. The module has zero callers in the frontend, the checker or compile_files. Source syntax: zero bit-field tokens anywhere in crates/qcore-frontend/, and the source record model carries no offsets or widths at all (crates/qcore-core/src/source_record.rs:107-110). C gateway: isBitfield is read at four sites purely to REFUSE, and the token reader refuses on the `:` character and discards the whole enclosing record.
CT10.why_still_unmapped: Mapping it would be mapping half a scenario, which wave 35 already declined and this lane declines on the same measured ground. The one shortcut available is the wrong answer for the right verdict: encoding two bit-fields of one byte as two leases of that byte, which the byte-granular mechanism would then refuse - the right verdict reached by a rule that knows nothing about bits, so a program whose bit-fields lay in DIFFERENT bytes would be admitted when C11 makes them one memory location only when they share a unit, and a program whose adjacent fields are addressable would be refused when they are genuinely independent. The scenario's own word is `bit-fields`, and the floor of every footprint in this workspace is one byte: an empty lease range is refused outright, so the interval can never be narrower. Closing this needs either a bit-field declaration in .qcore so a LayoutContract can be derived rather than hand-built, or DisjointFootprintsV1 wired to a source route at all. Both are route cards.

CT41.re_measured_on_this_tree: Not re-measured. Wave 35's CT-CTWIN-LANE measured it over five shapes through the real gateway entry points and declined it on a ground that is structural rather than a gap: the producer shapes with `volatile int g_done;` and with plain `int g_done;` are BYTE-IDENTICAL in verdict, reason and diagnostic, and the consumer shape is `safe` with no diagnostic at all. Identical verdicts across the volatile twins are the definition of failing clause (b) of the wave-9 attribution rule - removing the named construct must move the verdict, and here it moves nothing.
CT41.why_still_unmapped: This lane's charter says not to re-attempt without new capability, and there is none: the resource projection still has no synchronization model, and nothing in wave 36 or wave 37 gave it one. What IS new is a name for the premise on the gateway side - GATEWAY-VOLATILE-PREMISE, registered by wave 37's first arbiter - which is where a discharge would have to begin. Recorded so the decline is visible as a decision with a ground rather than as silence.
